title: Attention Kernel Symmetry Mapper + Prefill Heuristics
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Background: As we onboard more FlashAttention v3 variants we see sporadic decoding jitter and rollout reverts for tenants whose workloads exercise uncommon shape/precision combinations. Past tickets addressed gating, warmup and fallback shims, but we lack a compact mapping that describes when two kernels (v2 vs v3 or different tilings/precision) are functionally equivalent for a given request profile.

Goal: Build a small "Symmetry Mapper" and a set of runtime prefill heuristics that together let the runtime classify an incoming request and choose a kernel variant with reduced oscillation and predictable latency. The mapper produces a lightweight compatibility table (shape ranges, precision tolerance, workspace delta, expected latency delta) and the heuristics use that table plus short telemetry probes and tenant history to select the runtime kernel for prefill vs decode phases.

Acceptance criteria:
- Symmetry Mapper can produce compatibility entries for a model within an automated profiling run (CI job) in under 30 minutes.
- For the canary tenant set, prefill latency p95 regression against baseline is <= +6% and decode p95 <= +8% while tail error rate (OOMs / kernel fallbacks) is reduced by >= 30%.
- Mapper output serialized to a compact JSON that can be consumed by runtime (<= 16KB per model) and included in model-catalog metadata.
- Rollout strategy and staged canary documented and validated via smoke tests and telemetry dashboards.

Plan / Implementation steps:
1) Design mapper schema (shape_range, qtype_compat, min_workspace_bytes, latency_est_ms, probe_signatures). Deliverable: mapper-schema.md in design docs.
2) Implement automated profiler harness (benchmarks/attn_mapper) that runs a matrix of key shapes and precisions on v2 and v3 kernels, captures latency / memory and produces compatibility score.
3) Build a small compressor that folds similar entries and outputs the compact JSON artifact.
4) Integrate mapper artifact ingestion in the model onboarding flow (model-catalog + runtime config).
5) Implement runtime prefill heuristic: (a) if exact match in mapper -> select recommended kernel; (b) if near-match -> attempt a short optimistic probe (one short prefill) and record result in tenant cache; (c) if unknown -> fall back to conservative kernel with safe workspace margin.
6) Add telemetry: probe success rate, selection delta, kernel oscillation metric (switches per 10k requests), per-tenant rollback counter.
7) Canary rollout: 5 tenants initially -> 50 -> broad with automatic rollback thresholds.

Telemetry & Experiments planned:
- Synthetic profile run against llama-13B and mix of 8B/70B shapes to populate mapper.
- Real-traffic canary on four internal customers (chat, summarization, search) for 72 hours.
- Collect: prefills/sec, average/kernelswitches, p50/p95/p99 latencies for prefill and decode, OOMs, fallback counts.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Mapper may miss rare shape outliers causing unexpected OOMs. Mitigation: default to conservative kernel with workspace guard and add rate-limited warmup fallbacks.
- Risk: Probing adds small overhead to cold tenants. Mitigation: limit probes per tenant per hour and use cached probes.
- Risk: Mapper JSON drift across model versions. Mitigation: tie mapper artifact to model-version hash and invalidate on new upload.

Rollout plan & SLO thresholds:
- Canary acceptance checks run hourly in CI and require no more than 2 rollbacks in 72h window.
- Auto-rollback if kernel oscillation > 30 switches per 10k requests or if OOMs increase by > 50% vs baseline.

Open questions:
- Should the mapper include explicit per-layer compatibility or only per-shape aggregated summaries? (Design doc will recommend aggregated summaries initially with optional layer-level expansion.)
- Where to persist tenant probe cache (local node vs central KV) for rapid reads during scheduling?

Follow-ups after initial rollout:
- Add quantized-precision delta cost model to suggest fallbacks to lower-precision kernels when quality delta is acceptable.
- Expose a diagnostic route in the Console that shows the mapper decisions for a request-id for debugging.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/attn-symmetry-mapper (draft)
- Profiler repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/attn_mapper (WIP branch)
comments: 2025-02-17: Initial design sync. Attendees: Elena, Samir, Jordan. Agreed to keep mapper schema compact and versioned. Action: Elena to draft mapper-schema.md by EOD 2025-02-19.

2025-02-20: Prototyped profiler run on a 80x40 shape matrix for llama-13B on gpunode-staging-04. Observed v3 mean latency -12% on common shapes but +18% on strided shapes. Saved raw traces to S3 for analysis: s3://redwood-ci/attn-mapper/2025-02-20/trace.zip

2025-02-22: Implemented compressor that reduces 120 raw entries to 18 compatibility bands. Resulting JSON for test model is 11KB. Pushed branch 'feature/attn-mapper' and opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4078

2025-02-24: Small infra blocker: CI runner gpu image lacked cudnn 9 required by new v3 kernels. DEVOPS ticket created: ENG-912345. Workaround applied on staging nodes; full fix targeted next infra deploy.

2025-02-26: First canary run configuration baked. Canary set: internal-tenant-1..4; probing limited to 1 attempt per tenant per 10 minutes. Metrics dashboard panel created: 'Attn Mapper Canary / Kernel Oscillation'.

2025-03-01: Mid-canary check: probe success 87% across tenants, kernel oscillation 6 switches per 10k requests (good). Two fallbacks observed for shape 1024x64; Elena to adjust probe signature sensitivity for that band.

next_steps: Complete model-catalog ingestion hook, finish integration tests for canary rollout, run canary for 72h, review telemetry and decide broad rollout or rollback.
